sections.label: Geographical Indications Act and Registry
sections.summary: The Geographical Indications Act was enacted in 2014 and established the GI Registry agreed under the EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Geographical Indications Act (GI Act) was enacted in 2014 and established the GI Registry, which had been agreed to under the European Union (EU)-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (EUSFTA).

sections.label: Registered geographical indications count
sections.summary: As of 31 January 2020, 140 GIs have been registered.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As of 31 January 2020, 140 GIs have been registered.

sections.label: Technical amendments to GI Act
sections.summary: The Bill makes technical amendments to the GI Act to address issues from running the GI Registry and ensure smooth operations and clarity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill makes technical amendments to the GI Act to address issues that have arisen in the course of running the GI Registry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The amendments will ensure the continued smooth operations of the GI Registry and also provide greater clarity for traders and producers.

sections.label: Clause 5 QoR clarification
sections.summary: Clause 5 clarifies that a QoR may not be requested if it seeks qualification of all rights conferred on a registered GI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill, therefore, clarifies that a QoR may not be requested, if the QoR request seeks a qualification of all the rights to be conferred in respect of a registered GI.

sections.label: Post-registration QoR process removed
sections.summary: The Bill removes the post-registration QoR process and provides that post-registration limitation applications will be filed in and heard by the High Court.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, removes the post-registration QoR process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, provides that any post-registration applications for a limitation as to the scope of rights conferred in respect of a registered GI, will now be filed in and heard by the High Court, under a new judicial procedure called an application for a Limitation of Scope of rights in respect of a registered GI to be entered onto the Register.

sections.label: Bill implementation and GI Registry operations
sections.summary: The Bill's technical changes are targeted for implementation by the first half of this year, and in April 2019 the Act and registry operations began.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The changes sought under the Bill, as they are technical in nature and generally straightforward, are targeted to be implemented by the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In April 2019, the Geographical Indications Act 2014 came into effect, and, along with it, the registry of geographical indications started operations.

sections.label: Qualification of rights timing
sections.summary: Clause 5 amends the law so qualification of rights can only be made after publication but before registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On qualification of rights before registration, clause 5 amends the law so that qualification of rights can only be made after publication but before registration.

sections.label: Variants must meet GI criteria
sections.summary: Clause 4 clarifies variants must fulfil GI criteria to be registered, so variants are not a back-door option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill clarifies that variants need to fulfil the criteria of GI in order to be registered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This ensures that variants are not a back-door option for registering what was otherwise not registrable.

sections.label: GI Act 2014 registration system
sections.summary: The GI Act of 2014 established a registration system in Singapore from 1 April 2019, part of EUSFTA compliance, with some 100 applications protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The GI Act of 2014 established a new system of registration in Singapore to improve the certainty of protection given to GIs with effect from 1 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This had been part of Singapore's compliance with the EUSFTA where some 100 applications have been protected under the GI Act.

sections.label: 140 GI applications to IPOS
sections.summary: 140 GI applications have been made to IPOS since the GI Registry opened in April last year, but it is unclear how many are local.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to the same media report I cited earlier, and it is confirmed by the Senior Minister of State, 140 GI applications have been made to IPOS since the GI Registry was opened in April last year, but it is unclear how many are for local GIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Developing Singaporean GIs could be an avenue to boost the economic and job creation potential of the local food industry.

sections.label: Removing post-registration QoRs
sections.summary: Post-registration QoRs for registered GIs have been removed so the Registrar can reach registration decisions quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In handling these pending applications, it is in the interest of parties that the Registrar moves as quickly as possible to reach a registration decision, so that all parties are clear about the protection that is accorded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the other hand, after the GI is registered, post-registration matters can be independently handled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have, therefore, removed post-registration QoRs for registered GIs.

sections.label: Variant needs origin recognition
sections.summary: An applicant seeking to register a variant must show the variant has obtained recognition or registration as a GI in its country of origin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For a variant to be registered in Singapore, just as it is with any application for registration of a GI in Singapore, the applicant seeking to register a variant must show that the variant has obtained recognition or registration as a GI in its country of origin.

sections.label: Local applications breakdown request
sections.summary: Mr Leon Perera asked for the breakdown of local applications; the speaker lacks the number and will check and revert.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera asked what is the breakdown for local applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I do not have the number at hand but I will check and revert to Mr Perera.
